newsitem.title: UK: UK bank lending rises 3.53 bln stg in May.
newsitem.headline: UK bank lending rises 3.53 bln stg in May.

text.p: Total sterling lending by major British banks to the UK private sector rose a seasonally adjusted 3.53 billion stg in May, the British Bankers' Association said.
This figure was well up on the modest April increase of 1.192 billion and compares with the underlying six monthly average of 2.6 billion.
"Once again the strength of lending to persons was the outstanding feature in the major banks' figures for may," Tim Sweeney Director General of the BBA said.

"Whilst mortgage lending remained buoyant, it was the rise in consumer credit of approaching 600 million that is particularly eye-catching. This was around double the figure a year earlier and some 40 percent above the recent monthly average."

But he added that in part, the buoyancy of the banks' consumer lending earlier this year reflects an increase in market share. "It remains to be seen if the strength of the banks' lending in May will be reflected in the overall consumer credit figures for the month," he said.

Excluding investments and reverse repos, data show persons increased their borrowing by 1.392 billion stg in May, the highest monthly rise since the series began in 1991. In April by comparison, the figure was 1.263 billion.
Mortgage lending rose by 803 million stg up on both April's figure of 751 million and the six monthly average of 741 million.

Consumer credit rose by 594 million stg, including 196 million of lending on credit cards. The increase in consumer credit was the second highest rise since the series began and compares with the April figure of 515 million and a six monthly average of 431 million.

Lending to the financial sector rose by 900 million stg, down a little on the April increase of 981 million. Within the total notable rises were recorded by leasing company -- 427 million stg, building societies -- 349 million and insurance companies and pension funds -- 186 million.
Lending to the manufacturing sector rose by 227 million and, within this, the other manufacturing sector recorded a marked rise of 162 million.
Elsewhere in the company sector, there were notable rises for other services, up 351 million stg, largely representing take-over finance.
